brief: Mag 7 implied vol trades at a steep discount to the broader tech complex, with the relative vol ratio at just the 15th percentile over four years. Yet the NDX/SPX implied vol spread, despite compressing sharply over three days (the largest compression in four years) after last week's blowout, still sits at the 94th percentile, so tech vol stays historically expensive versus the S&P 500 beneath that Mag 7 discount. Underneath, skew remains well bid and vol-of-vol has swung violently since mid-October, with downside protection still in demand. Nomura's McElligott flags aggressive Mag 7 upside call buying ahead of earnings (AAPL, GOOGL, MSFT, about $1.6bn combined delta) alongside a positioning split: hedge fund Mag 7 beta near the 97th percentile historically versus mutual funds near the 11th. Goldman, treating the resetting vol as an opportunity to add upside, likes AMZN Dec 280/310 call spreads into earnings (citing a July deleveraging analog when AMZN surged 15% on earnings), SPY November $780 calls for potential clearing events, and EWY December 180/210 call spreads on a Korea AI-momentum squeeze after heavy hedge fund de-risking.
